strings.IME_THENEWORDER_DESC: When the Italian Empire expanded at a breakneck pace during World War Two, few among the fascist leadership stopped to consider the fact that some of the newly conquered territories would have been more trouble than they were worth. In the Levant, Italian rule was constantly marked by fierce resistance by native Arabs, and the plans to counterbalance them with Jewish immigrants backfired as Zionist groups took up arms against Italy as well. Dalla Chiesa, the new young Governor, adopted a new strategy - attempting to negotiate with moderate of both camps, which fostered an uneasy peace between the Italians, Haganah and Fatah. The threat of Turkey looms on the horizon, and it might be the only thing capable of uniting the peoples of the Levant, or to once and for all doom the region to chaos.

strings.IME_italys_finest_desc: Under the strong but fair leadership of Governor-General dalla Chiesa, our armed forces are some of the best in the Italian sphere. With the constant need to put down rebellions from both the Zionists and Palestinians, our troops have become accustomed to conditions and the fighting style in the Middle East.
strings.IME_haganah_fatah_negotiations_desc: Given the extreme ineffectiveness of the more classic methods of Italian colonialism, the Italian authorities in the Levant have been forced to negotiate with the two major political and paramilitary organizations in the region, Haganah and Fatah, as an attempt to keep the Levant stable. Haganah is a self-defense militia dedicated to protecting Jewish settlements in Palestine, with Italy's approval, while Fatah is a larger Arab organization and paramilitary who has campaigned for the independence of the Levant as an independent Arab state. While both are somewhat willing to tolerate cooperation with the Italian government to pursue their own goals, they don't enjoy a great relationship between each other, and the uneasy peace that was reached between Italy, the Jews and the Arabs is constantly at risk of falling apart.
strings.IME_terrorism_desc: Despite Italy's efforts to find a mostly non violent solution to Levantine unrest, there are still many in the region who fiercely oppose the Italian government. Among the Jews, those who were displeased by Haganah's moderation formed Irgun, a revisionist Zionist paramilitary group who fights for a Jewish state that spans the whole Levant, and isn't afraid to attack Italians and Arabs alike in their pursuit. Among the Arabs, the Harakiyyin, or ANM, was formed as a loose coalition of numerous communist, left wing nationalist and other groups, all campaigning for an independent Arab Levant, attacking both the Italian imperialists and their perceived Zionist puppets. Together, these groups have proved a major thorn in the side of the Italian government, and spread terror and fear among the population with their attacks on Italian soldiers and civilians alike.
strings.IME_emirate_of_transjordan_desc: While the Italian administration in the Levant focuses on maintaining an uneasy peace in the western part of the Governorate, the lands beyond the River Jordan make up the Emirate of Transjordan. Effectively a vassal state of Italy, Transjordan has her own armed forces (albeit commanded by Italian officers), her own government (albeit heavily dependent on the Italian one), and her own ruler, Emir Hussein bin Talal, who has been more than happy to collaborate with Italy for the lucrative oil deals which can be found in working with ENI, providing him with enough wealth to modernize and develop his realm. In more recent times, Emir Hussein has become a supporter of Fatah, especially of its more traditionalist and moderate wing, and his deep pockets have become a major source of funding for the organization, drawing some concern from the Italians.
